style.vernacular: Ancient walled Hausa city in the Sudano-Sahelian tubali tradition: ochre-brown mud-render (laterite-and-straw) compounds with flat roofs, horn-like corner pinnacles (zankwaye) and a decorated gatehouse (zaure) at each house; the old city is ringed by earth walls about 9 m high with gates (kofa); outside it, colonial Sabon Gari and Nassarawa have painted-sandcrete shophouses and bungalows, and the modern city is concrete and corrugated tin under neem and date palms on dusty laterite.
style.ornament: Hausa facade relief (zane) hand-carved in mud or cement render around the zaure and doors: interlaced knots (dagi), staff-of-office and sword motifs, geometric bands; horn-like corner pinnacles (zankwaye) and crenellated parapets on palace, gates and mosques; indigo-dyed cloth hung in the old city; hand-painted shop signs.

sources.what: Sudanian savanna Koppen Aw climate, ~480 m elevation, Tubali Sudano-Sahelian architecture, city walls begun by King Gijimasu and about 30 ft (9 m) high in Barth 1851, most gates survive
laterite earth walls plastered, relief decoration surface designs/ornament/calligraphy, rain erosion, tin mosque roofs

style.vernacular: Lagoon city of towers and low-rise: the Plateau CBD has 1970s-80s concrete and glass office towers (Little Manhattan) over the Ebrie Lagoon; Cocody, Marcory and Treichville are 2-4 storey painted-render blocks, colonial-era grid streets and villas with corrugated or tile roofs, set among palms and broadleaf trees on humid, red-brown ground.
style.ornament: Modernist monuments with strong geometry (triangular cathedral, tall concrete cross), brise-soleil and balcony bands on 1970s blocks, colourful ceramic panels and Ivorian motifs, Fokker-plane and lagoon-front landmarks; white and orange-white-green national colours on public buildings.

sources.what: Plateau skyscrapers and CCIA tower (1982), Cocody colonial-style villas, Treichville colonial grid, tropical wet-dry Koppen Aw climate, Banco forest
